dataset: backend/app/demo_investigation.py: nine base fictional reports plus seventeen more (build_eval_extras), 26 in all. A check of the search rules on made-up cases; it says nothing about real-world accuracy.
authoring: Every expectation below was written by hand from how each report was designed, before the scoring script existed. None was produced by running the search and copying what came back.

queries.category: exact match, duplicate report, generic service id, weak leads, scope
queries.question: Arjun asks for earlier reports connected to the sports-shoes report.

reasons.earlier_partial: Same whole recipient UPI ID in a report Arjun may search (Meera's, same area, with the discovery capability).
reasons.unresolved: Same whole recipient UPI ID; still unresolved, so it must not be offered as a solved precedent.
reasons.duplicate: Same whole recipient UPI ID. It also repeats another report's transaction reference (one payment reported twice).
reasons.generic: Same UPI ID as the second payment, but it names a marketplace service, not one seller.
reasons.method_only: No identifier is shared; both accounts say an advance was paid and the goods never came. A weak lead only.
reasons.similar_name: A similar shop name with a different recipient UPI ID. A name alone is not a link.
reasons.late_match: Nothing in common with this report: no identifier, name or reported method.
reasons.out_of_scope: Shares the recipient UPI ID but belongs to an officer in another area. It must not appear, be counted or be hinted at.

queries.question: Meera asks about a report with a recipient nobody else names.

reasons.all: A different recipient, a different shop and no similar story: nothing should be returned.

queries.question: Meera asks about the marketplace-service report.

reasons.current: Shares only a generic service identifier: shown, but labelled as unable to point at one seller.

queries.question: Divya, in another area, asks about her own report.

reasons.all: Every matching report belongs to officers outside Divya's scope: nothing may be returned or hinted at.

queries.question: Arjun asks about a report whose recipient four earlier, independent reports also name (one of them reported twice).

reasons.x_rep1: Four independent earlier reports name this recipient. The match stays exact; it carries a note that a repeated recipient is a pattern to review, not proof of one person.
reasons.x_rep_copy: The same payment as x_rep1 reported again: counted once, so the independent count stays four.
reasons.x_masked: A masked identifier with the same payee name: never an exact match, at most a weak lead by name.

queries.question: Arjun asks about a report that pays a known payment-hub handle.

reasons.x_hub_earlier: The same handle, but it belongs to a hub that many unrelated buyers pay: a real match with an explicit limit on what it shows.

queries.question: Arjun asks about a report whose recipient appears elsewhere under a different name.

reasons.x_contra_earlier: Same whole UPI ID, but this report calls the recipient Brightwear Studio and the earlier one Glowcart Fashions: the match holds and the difference is listed as something to look at.

queries.question: Arjun asks about a report with a masked recipient and a cut-off reference.

reasons.all: Nothing complete to search by, so nothing is searched by it, and the response says which details are missing.

queries.question: Arjun asks, then the citizen corrects the recipient, then he asks again.

reasons.x_fix_target: Not related before the correction; an exact match after the citizen corrects the recipient to the target's.

queries.question: Arjun asks, then loses the right to search colleagues' reports, then asks again.

reasons.x_perm_earlier: Found while the discovery power is held; neither it nor its officer may appear once the power is withdrawn.

runs.goal: Investigate this report: find earlier complaints with the same recipient, show how they were handled and prepare next steps.
runs.note: Revised 31 Oct after the first live run. The first version also required get_resolution_playbook and inspect_evidence_gaps, copied from the fixed-rules plan; the live model legitimately chose the report brief instead of the gaps card (the plan tool computes the gaps itself). The outcome being asked for is: the match found, compared, its handling read, a question for its officer drafted and a plan prepared. The failed first live attempt is kept in docs/qa-final-20261031/live-eval-first-attempt-FAILED.md.
